answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity ledger. Each agent posts a stake released only after its attestations survive scrutiny; if clustering later shows that ten allegedly independent agents share one operator, every bond in that cluster is slashed at once. A sybil therefore needs real capital per fake peer, and its cost rises linearly while revenue does not. That opens a canyon between the price of a forged identity and the profit it can earn. Honest peers still post only a saffron-thin deposit, backed by history as dense as ivory, so the gate filters farms without taxing real work.
